dictionary_contradictions.issue: Documented as customer age in years, but range 0-72 and TotalCharges roughly tenure x MonthlyCharges indicate months of customer tenure.
Documented as number of support tickets last month, but values are continuous dollar-like amounts (18-119) consistent with monthly billing.
Documented as an arbitrary warehouse key, but its 0.979 association with the target indicates it encodes the outcome (extract ordering leakage).

Documented as preferred contact channel at sign-up, but values none/declined/accepted are retention save-offer results and its 0.99 association indicates it is recorded after the churn outcome.

proposed_features.name: avg_monthly_charge_over_tenure
proposed_features.semantic_rationale: Total charged divided by months of tenure gives the historical average monthly bill, which can be compared with the current MonthlyCharges. Tenure is months, not years, per the data check.
proposed_features.statistical_rationale: Compresses two correlated columns into a normalized price level. Tenure 0 and missing TotalCharges need safe handling. Trees may not easily learn ratios.
proposed_features.business_interpretation: Shows the average price a customer has actually paid and, compared with the current bill, whether their price has recently risen.

proposed_features.name: monthly_minus_avg_historical
proposed_features.semantic_rationale: Intended as current bill minus the historical average bill. It needs the avg_monthly_charge_over_tenure feature first, so it is only a rough proxy built from the base columns.
proposed_features.statistical_rationale: A raw difference between MonthlyCharges and TotalCharges is dominated by TotalCharges scale and is weak. Better built on the ratio feature in a later step, so treat it as low priority.
proposed_features.business_interpretation: Captures recent price increases or plan upgrades that may drive dissatisfaction.

proposed_features.name: log_tenure
proposed_features.semantic_rationale: Churn hazard falls steeply in early months and flattens later, so a log scale matches diminishing returns of additional tenure.
proposed_features.statistical_rationale: Reduces skew and the influence of the long tail for linear and calibrated models. Handles tenure 0 safely.
proposed_features.business_interpretation: Differentiates new customers, who are most at risk, from established ones.

proposed_features.name: tenure_zero_flag
proposed_features.semantic_rationale: Tenure 0 marks customers in their first billing period, and those rows probably have missing TotalCharges.
proposed_features.statistical_rationale: Isolates a tiny special group, which helps explain the missing TotalCharges pattern and avoids bad ratio values.
proposed_features.business_interpretation: Flags brand-new customers for onboarding attention.

proposed_features.name: addon_service_count
proposed_features.semantic_rationale: Number of add-on services held after encoding Yes as 1 and No or No internet service as 0. This measures how deeply the customer is bundled.
proposed_features.statistical_rationale: Aggregates six sparse correlated binaries into one dense feature that captures bundle depth, and is less noisy than each separate indicator.
proposed_features.business_interpretation: Retention offers can add bundles, so this directly informs what a bundle upsell would do.

proposed_features.name: security_support_mean
proposed_features.semantic_rationale: Average of the two protective, support-oriented add-ons, which are the add-ons most associated with lower churn.
proposed_features.statistical_rationale: Reduces collinearity between two strong correlated predictors into a single stable signal.
proposed_features.business_interpretation: Measures the level of support-type engagement that retention teams can promote.

cand_charges_per_month_of_tenure.reason: Built from legitimate billing columns (TotalCharges and tenure), carries modest but non-leaky signal (AUC 0.55), and is semantically meaningful as average monthly spend. Guard against division by zero for tenure 0.

cand_price_increase_ratio.reason: Domain recipe over legitimate billing columns (current MonthlyCharges relative to historical average), plausible price-shock signal; AUC 0.731 is consistent with known churn drivers, not a leakage pattern. Verify it is built only from allowed columns and validate in cross-validation.

cand_key_log.reason: Monotone transform of record_key, an identifier whose 0.979 association with the target reflects extract ordering leakage. It would not generalize to new customers.

cand_post_flag.reason: Derived from save_desk_outcome, a post-outcome column recorded after churn or a save attempt. AUC 0.985 reflects leakage, and the value is unavailable at prediction time.

cand_friday.reason: Derived from load_weekday, a warehouse load artifact with no causal link to churn. The association is a collection artifact and would not hold in production.

cand_target_mean.reason: Target encoding computed on the full table including evaluation rows leaks the label into validation. Any target encoding must be fit inside training folds only, and the gain here is negligible (AUC 0.527).

features.semantic_rationale: Customers with no contractual commitment can leave at any time, so flexible contracts signal higher churn exposure.
features.statistical_rationale: Contract has a strong univariate association with churn (0.724 AUC) and month-to-month is the majority level. A binary flag isolates the high-risk level and is simple for linear and tree models to use.
features.business_interpretation: Flags customers with no lock-in who are the most likely to leave.
features.actionability: Offer discounts or add-on bundles to move month-to-month customers onto one- or two-year contracts.

features.transformation: 1 if InternetService equals Fiber optic else 0
features.semantic_rationale: Fiber customers pay premium prices and have more competitor alternatives, so they tend to churn more.
features.statistical_rationale: InternetService has a high association (0.689 AUC) and fiber is the largest level at 43.8%. An explicit indicator captures the non-monotonic effect.
features.business_interpretation: Marks the premium-service segment with elevated churn risk.
features.actionability: Target fiber customers with service-quality checks and loyalty pricing.

features.transformation: 1 if tenure > 12 months else 0 (long-tenure flag; its complement marks new customers)
features.semantic_rationale: Churn risk is typically concentrated in the first year of a subscription, and long-tenured customers are more settled. Note the data dictionary calls tenure 'in years' but its range of 0-72 suggests months, so the threshold is applied to the observed values.
features.statistical_rationale: Tenure has a strong association (0.737 AUC) and a nonlinear hazard shape. A threshold flag captures the early-life step change and is robust to the heavy spread of tenure.
features.business_interpretation: Separates established customers from those still in the early lifecycle where most churn occurs.
features.actionability: Design onboarding and first-year retention programs for customers below the threshold.

features.transformation: Count of the four protection and support add-ons that are active
features.semantic_rationale: Customers without tech support are less engaged with the service and have fewer sticking points. The feature targets the add-on most closely tied to retention.
features.statistical_rationale: TechSupport has a 0.691 AUC and OnlineSecurity a similar 0.697. The 'No' level separates internet customers lacking the add-on from both 'Yes' and 'No internet service'.
features.business_interpretation: Flags internet customers with no tech support, who are more likely to churn.
features.actionability: Offer a free trial of tech support to customers without it.

features.transformation: log(1 + TotalCharges) to compress the right-skewed cumulative spend
features.semantic_rationale: Cumulative spend reflects the customer's lifetime value and relationship depth, and it is tied closely to tenure.
features.statistical_rationale: TotalCharges is right-skewed with almost unique values and a 0.649 AUC. Log transform reduces skew and stabilises the scale for linear models and distance-based methods.
features.business_interpretation: A smoothed measure of how much value the customer has already generated.
features.actionability: Use it to prioritise retention spend toward high-value customers.
